title: Acts Chapter 13 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Acts chapter 13 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Acts Chapter 13 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Acts Chapter 13.

questions.question: In Acts 13, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Barnabas and Saul were sent for the work God called them to
Certain prophets and teachers were in the church at Antioch
Paul and his company sailed to Cyprus
Elymas the sorcerer opposed Barnabas and Saul
questions.correctAnswer: Certain prophets and teachers were in the church at Antioch
questions.explanation: Acts 13:1 mentions first that there were certain prophets and teachers in the church at Antioch before any other events.

questions.question: Who were some of the prophets and teachers in the church at Antioch?
options: Barnabas, Simeon called Niger, Lucius of Cyrene, Manaen, and Saul
Peter, John, James, and Paul
Barnabas, Silas, Timothy, and Paul
James, John, Judas, and Simon
questions.correctAnswer: Barnabas, Simeon called Niger, Lucius of Cyrene, Manaen, and Saul
questions.explanation: Acts 13:1 lists these men specifically as prophets and teachers in the church at Antioch.

questions.question: What did the Holy Ghost say while they ministered and fasted?
options: Separate me Barnabas and Saul for the work whereunto I have called them
Go preach to all nations
Build a new church in Antioch
Send Paul to Jerusalem immediately
questions.correctAnswer: Separate me Barnabas and Saul for the work whereunto I have called them
questions.explanation: Acts 13:2 records the Holy Ghost saying this during their ministry and fasting.

questions.question: What did the church do after the Holy Ghost instructed them about Barnabas and Saul?
options: They fasted, prayed, laid hands on them, and sent them away
They immediately sent them without prayer
They asked them to stay longer
They told them to go alone without any support
questions.correctAnswer: They fasted, prayed, laid hands on them, and sent them away
questions.explanation: Acts 13:3 states that after fasting and praying, they laid hands on Barnabas and Saul and sent them away.

questions.question: Where did Barnabas and Saul sail to after departing from Antioch?
options: Cyprus
Jerusalem
Rome
Ephesus
questions.correctAnswer: Cyprus
questions.explanation: Acts 13:4 says they departed to Seleucia and then sailed to Cyprus.

questions.question: Who was with Barnabas and Saul as their minister when they preached in Salamis?
options: John
Peter
James
Timothy
questions.correctAnswer: John
questions.explanation: Acts 13:5 mentions John was their minister while they preached in the synagogues at Salamis.

questions.question: What was the name of the sorcerer and false prophet they encountered in Paphos?
options: Barjesus
Elymas
Manaen
Sergius Paulus
questions.correctAnswer: Barjesus
questions.explanation: Acts 13:6 gives the name of the sorcerer as Barjesus.

questions.question: Who was Sergius Paulus?
options: The deputy of the country who was a prudent man
A Jewish priest
The king of Cyprus
A prophet in the church at Antioch
questions.correctAnswer: The deputy of the country who was a prudent man
questions.explanation: Acts 13:7 describes Sergius Paulus as the deputy of the country and a prudent man.

questions.question: What did Elymas the sorcerer try to do?
options: Withstand Barnabas and Saul and turn away the deputy from the faith
Help Barnabas and Saul preach
Lead the deputy to believe in Jesus
Join the church in Antioch
questions.correctAnswer: Withstand Barnabas and Saul and turn away the deputy from the faith
questions.explanation: Acts 13:8 states Elymas sought to turn away the deputy from the faith by opposing them.

questions.question: What happened to Elymas after Paul, filled with the Holy Ghost, confronted him?
options: He was blinded and went about seeking someone to lead him by the hand
He was arrested and imprisoned
He repented and believed
He fled the country
questions.correctAnswer: He was blinded and went about seeking someone to lead him by the hand
questions.explanation: Acts 13:11 describes Elymas being struck blind and needing someone to lead him.

questions.question: What was the reaction of the deputy Sergius Paulus after Elymas was blinded?
options: He believed and was astonished at the doctrine of the Lord
He became angry and expelled Barnabas and Saul
He ignored the event
He called for a public debate
questions.correctAnswer: He believed and was astonished at the doctrine of the Lord
questions.explanation: Acts 13:12 records that Sergius Paulus believed and was amazed at the teaching of the Lord.

questions.question: Where did Paul and his company go after leaving Paphos?
options: Perga in Pamphylia
Jerusalem
Antioch in Pisidia
Seleucia
questions.correctAnswer: Perga in Pamphylia
questions.explanation: Acts 13:13 says they came to Perga in Pamphylia after leaving Paphos.

questions.question: True or False: Manaen was brought up with Herod the tetrarch.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Acts 13:1 states Manaen had been brought up with Herod the tetrarch.

questions.question: True or False: Paul stood up and addressed the men of Israel and those who fear God in the synagogue.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Acts 13:16 describes Paul standing up and beckoning to the men of Israel and those that fear God to listen.

questions.question: True or False: The text says Elymas was immediately imprisoned after being struck blind.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Acts 13:11 only says Elymas was blinded and went about seeking someone to lead him, with no mention of imprisonment.

medium.title: Acts Chapter 13 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Acts Chapter 13 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Acts 13:19, what did God do after destroying seven nations in the land of Canaan?
options: He divided their land to them by lot
He made a covenant with them
He sent prophets to guide them
He built a temple for them
questions.correctAnswer: He divided their land to them by lot
questions.explanation: Acts 13:19 states that after God destroyed seven nations, He divided their land to the Israelites by lot.

questions.question: What does Acts 13:20 promise will happen if someone follows the judges God gave to Israel?
options: They will be led for about four hundred and fifty years
They will inherit the land of Canaan immediately
They will become kings and rulers
They will be delivered from their enemies
questions.correctAnswer: They will be led for about four hundred and fifty years
questions.explanation: Acts 13:20 refers to the period of judges leading Israel for about 450 years after the land was divided (Acts 13:19).

questions.question: According to Acts 13:23, who has God raised up as a Saviour according to His promise?
options: Jesus
Samuel
David
John the Baptist
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus
questions.explanation: Acts 13:23 clearly states that God has raised up Jesus as a Saviour according to His promise.

questions.question: How do Acts 13:27 and Acts 13:28 relate in explaining the reaction of Jerusalem's rulers to Jesus?
options: They knew Him not and desired Pilate to have Him slain
They welcomed Him as their king
They ignored the prophets' voices
They immediately believed in Him
questions.correctAnswer: They knew Him not and desired Pilate to have Him slain
questions.explanation: Acts 13:27 explains that rulers in Jerusalem did not know Jesus nor the prophets, and Acts 13:28 states they desired Pilate to kill Him despite finding no cause of death.

questions.question: What practical lesson can Christians learn from John’s humility as described in Acts 13:25?
options: True humility recognizes one's role in God's plan without seeking personal glory
Leaders should always seek recognition for their work
It is important to boast about one’s authority
John refused to acknowledge Jesus' coming
questions.correctAnswer: True humility recognizes one's role in God's plan without seeking personal glory
questions.explanation: Acts 13:25 shows John saying he is not the one to come but points to the one after him, demonstrating humility and submission to God's plan.

questions.question: According to Acts 13:26, to whom is the word of salvation sent?
options: Men and brethren, children of Abraham, and whosoever fears God
Only the Jewish elders
Only the Gentiles
Only those born in Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: Men and brethren, children of Abraham, and whosoever fears God
questions.explanation: Acts 13:26 states the word of salvation is sent to the children of Abraham and anyone who fears God.

questions.question: What does Acts 13:34 promise concerning Jesus after His resurrection?
options: He will no longer return to corruption and will provide the sure mercies of David
He will return to Jerusalem to reign immediately
He will suffer again for the people's sins
He will be forgotten as all men perish
questions.correctAnswer: He will no longer return to corruption and will provide the sure mercies of David
questions.explanation: Acts 13:34 explains that Jesus was raised from the dead never to see corruption and will give the sure mercies of David.

questions.question: What practical encouragement does the resurrection of Jesus in Acts 13:30 provide to believers?
options: God has power over death, giving hope for eternal life
Death is the end of all things
Resurrection is uncertain and not promised
Jesus was raised only temporarily
questions.correctAnswer: God has power over death, giving hope for eternal life
questions.explanation: Acts 13:30 states God raised Jesus from the dead, demonstrating power over death and providing hope for believers.

questions.question: How does Acts 13:22 describe God's testimony about David?
options: A man after mine own heart, which shall fulfil all my will
A man who failed God's purpose
A king who ruled without God's favor
A prophet who spoke lies
questions.correctAnswer: A man after mine own heart, which shall fulfil all my will
questions.explanation: Acts 13:22 quotes God testifying that David was a man after His own heart who would accomplish His will.

questions.question: What does Acts 13:29 reveal about the fulfillment of prophecy concerning Jesus' death?
options: All that was written of Him was fulfilled when He was taken down from the tree and laid in a sepulchre
Jesus escaped death and remained alive
Prophecies were not fulfilled in His death
He was buried in an unknown place
questions.correctAnswer: All that was written of Him was fulfilled when He was taken down from the tree and laid in a sepulchre
questions.explanation: Acts 13:29 states that Jesus' death and burial fulfilled all Scripture written about Him.

questions.question: Based on Acts 13:24, what was John's role before Jesus' coming?
options: Preaching the baptism of repentance to all Israel
Leading a rebellion
Performing miracles to prove himself
Teaching Gentiles exclusively
questions.correctAnswer: Preaching the baptism of repentance to all Israel
questions.explanation: Acts 13:24 describes John as preaching a baptism of repentance before Jesus' arrival.

questions.question: How can believers apply the message in Acts 13:26 to their own lives today?
options: By accepting the word of salvation if they fear God, regardless of background
By only listening to those from Abraham's lineage
By rejecting the message unless it is from a synagogue
By focusing solely on good works
questions.correctAnswer: By accepting the word of salvation if they fear God, regardless of background
questions.explanation: Acts 13:26 extends the message of salvation to all who fear God, encouraging openness to God’s word beyond ethnic boundaries.

questions.question: What lesson about spiritual leadership can be drawn from Acts 13:21 regarding Israel's desire for a king?
options: God responds to the people's requests by providing leadership, even if it departs from His judges
Leaders should never be appointed by the people
God ignores the desires of His people
Kingship is always the best form of leadership
questions.correctAnswer: God responds to the people's requests by providing leadership, even if it departs from His judges
questions.explanation: Acts 13:21 shows that after judges, Israel desired a king, and God provided Saul to lead them for 40 years.

questions.question: True or False: Acts 13:31 indicates that Jesus was seen by many witnesses after His resurrection.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Acts 13:31 states that Jesus was seen many days by those who came with Him from Galilee to Jerusalem, serving as witnesses.

questions.question: True or False: Acts 13:35 claims that David's body did not see corruption after death.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Acts 13:35 says 'Thou shalt not suffer thine Holy One to see corruption,' referring to Jesus, while Acts 13:36 clarifies David did see corruption after death.

hard.title: Acts Chapter 13 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Acts Chapter 13.

questions.question: According to Acts 13:37, what is significant about the one whom God raised again?
options: Saw no corruption
Was immediately glorified
Ascended to heaven
Spoke in tongues
questions.correctAnswer: Saw no corruption
questions.explanation: Acts 13:37 states 'But he, whom God raised again, saw no corruption,' emphasizing the resurrection without decay.

questions.question: In Acts 13:38, what is preached through Jesus according to Paul?
options: The forgiveness of sins
The law of Moses
Eternal judgment
The kingdom of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The forgiveness of sins
questions.explanation: Acts 13:38 says, 'Be it known unto you therefore, men and brethren, that through this man is preached unto you the forgiveness of sins,' showing the core message of salvation.

questions.question: What justification is mentioned in Acts 13:39 that believers receive through Christ?
options: Justified from all things from which the law of Moses could not justify
Justified by keeping the law perfectly
Justified by works of righteousness
Justified by offerings and sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: Justified from all things from which the law of Moses could not justify
questions.explanation: Acts 13:39 states, 'And by him all that believe are justified from all things, from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses,' indicating justification by faith, not the law.

questions.question: What warning does Paul give in Acts 13:40?
options: Beware lest that come upon you which is spoken of in the prophets
Beware of false teachers among you
Beware of worldly riches
Beware of speaking against the synagogue rulers
questions.correctAnswer: Beware lest that come upon you which is spoken of in the prophets
questions.explanation: Acts 13:40 says, 'Beware therefore, lest that come upon you, which is spoken of in the prophets;' warning listeners to heed prophetic judgment.

questions.question: Acts 13:41 contains a quotation from the prophets. What is the reaction of those addressed as 'despisers' to the work God is doing?
options: They wonder and perish
They rejoice and believe
They remain silent
They celebrate publicly
questions.correctAnswer: They wonder and perish
questions.explanation: Acts 13:41 says, 'Behold, ye despisers, and wonder, and perish: for I work a work in your days,' indicating disbelief leads to destruction.

questions.question: What happened after the Jews left the synagogue in Acts 13:42?
options: The Gentiles asked that the word be preached to them the next sabbath
Paul and Barnabas left the city immediately
The synagogue elders invited Paul to teach privately
The crowd dispersed without interest
questions.correctAnswer: The Gentiles asked that the word be preached to them the next sabbath
questions.explanation: Acts 13:42 states, 'And when the Jews were gone out of the synagogue, the Gentiles besought that these words might be preached to them the next sabbath,' showing Gentile interest.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'dikaioo' in Acts 13:39 mean?
options: To justify or declare righteous
To condemn or judge
To sanctify or make holy
To forgive or pardon
questions.correctAnswer: To justify or declare righteous
questions.explanation: 'Dikaioo' used in Acts 13:39 means 'to justify or declare righteous' in a legal sense, referring to acquittal from guilt before God.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Acts 13:34-37 to contrast David and Jesus?
options: Typology
Chiasm
Parallelism
Allegory
questions.correctAnswer: Typology
questions.explanation: Acts 13:34-37 uses typology by presenting David as a type whose death contrasts with Jesus' resurrection without corruption, foreshadowing Christ's victory.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage does Paul quote in Acts 13:35 about the Holy One not seeing corruption?
options: Psalm 16:10
Isaiah 53:5
Exodus 12:46
Genesis 3:15
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 16:10
questions.explanation: Acts 13:35 references Psalm 16:10, 'Thou shalt not suffer thine Holy One to see corruption,' used to support Jesus' resurrection.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of justification by faith rather than law as in Acts 13:39?
options: Romans 3:28
Matthew 5:17
John 14:6
Galatians 5:16
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 3:28
questions.explanation: Romans 3:28 states, 'Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law,' echoing Acts 13:39's theme of justification beyond the Mosaic law.

questions.question: Before Paul preached about forgiveness of sins in Acts 13:38, what historical summary does he give in Acts 13:17-22?
options: The history of Israel from Egypt to David
The genealogies of the tribes of Israel
The laws given on Mount Sinai
The exile and return from Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: The history of Israel from Egypt to David
questions.explanation: Acts 13:17-22 summarizes Israel's history from the Exodus out of Egypt through the period of judges to King David, setting the stage for Jesus' coming.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes the words in Acts 13:47 where Paul and Barnabas say they turn to the Gentiles?
options: The Jews rejecting the message and judging themselves unworthy of eternal life
The healing of a lame man at the temple
The baptism of new converts
The casting out of a demon
questions.correctAnswer: The Jews rejecting the message and judging themselves unworthy of eternal life
questions.explanation: Acts 13:46 says, 'seeing ye put it from you, and judge yourselves unworthy of everlasting life, lo, we turn to the Gentiles,' showing rejection precedes the turning.

questions.question: What cultural practice is implied by Paul and Barnabas 'shaking off the dust of their feet' in Acts 13:51?
options: A symbolic act of disassociation from a hostile city
A ritual cleansing before entering a synagogue
A gesture of blessing on the city
A method to remove physical dirt after travel
questions.correctAnswer: A symbolic act of disassociation from a hostile city
questions.explanation: Acts 13:51 shows Paul and Barnabas shaking the dust off their feet as a Jewish custom symbolizing rejection of and disassociation from those who oppose the gospel.

questions.question: How does Acts 13:50 demonstrate the sociopolitical challenges faced by early Christian missionaries?
options: Jews stirred up influential women and leaders to persecute Paul and Barnabas
Roman authorities immediately arrested the missionaries
Local pagan priests embraced the gospel
Synagogue rulers welcomed the new teaching
questions.correctAnswer: Jews stirred up influential women and leaders to persecute Paul and Barnabas
questions.explanation: Acts 13:50 describes Jews provoking devout women and chief city men to persecute and expel Paul and Barnabas, showing early opposition from religious and social elites.

questions.question: What is the emotional and spiritual state of the disciples after Paul and Barnabas arrive in Iconium according to Acts 13:52?
options: They were filled with joy and the Holy Ghost
They were fearful and discouraged
They were silent and confused
They withdrew from the community
questions.correctAnswer: They were filled with joy and the Holy Ghost
questions.explanation: Acts 13:52 states, 'And the disciples were filled with joy, and with the Holy Ghost,' indicating spiritual empowerment despite persecution.

theological.title: Acts Chapter 13 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Acts Chapter 13 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 13:38 teach about salvation?
options: Forgiveness of sins is preached through Jesus
Salvation is earned by adherence to the law
Forgiveness is granted by human works
Salvation is limited to ethnic Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Forgiveness of sins is preached through Jesus
questions.explanation: Acts 13:38 states that through this man (Jesus) forgiveness of sins is preached, indicating salvation comes through Him and not by law or works.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 13:39 teach about justification?
options: Believers are justified from all things through Jesus, not by the law of Moses
Justification is only possible through strict law observance
Only the circumcised can be justified
Justification is a result of ritual sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are justified from all things through Jesus, not by the law of Moses
questions.explanation: Acts 13:39 clearly teaches that justification comes through faith in Jesus and not by the Mosaic law.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 13:22 teach concerning God's election and leadership?
options: God removes and raises up leaders according to His will
Kingship is determined by popular vote
Leadership depends on military power
God abandons leaders when they fail
questions.correctAnswer: God removes and raises up leaders according to His will
questions.explanation: Acts 13:22 states that God removed Saul and raised up David as king, showing divine sovereignty in leadership.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Acts 13:11 specifically demonstrate?
options: Judgment
Omniscience
Immanence
Justice
questions.correctAnswer: Judgment
questions.explanation: Acts 13:11 shows God's judgment as Elymas is struck blind for opposing the gospel.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Acts 13:33 specifically demonstrate?
options: Faithfulness to promise
Wrath
Omnipotence
Immutability
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness to promise
questions.explanation: Acts 13:33 shows God fulfilling the promise to the fathers by raising Jesus from the dead, demonstrating His faithfulness.

questions.question: How does Acts 13:24–25 prepare for the fulfillment of messianic prophecy in the New Testament?
options: By showing John's role as forerunner pointing to Christ
By emphasizing the irrelevance of John the Baptist
By denying the necessity of repentance
By showing Jesus as a political revolutionary
questions.correctAnswer: By showing John's role as forerunner pointing to Christ
questions.explanation: Verses 24–25 describe John preaching repentance and pointing to the coming one, preparing for Christ's arrival.

questions.question: How does Acts 13:46–47 fulfill the theme of mission to the Gentiles in redemptive history?
options: It shows the word of God turning from Jews to Gentiles as commanded by the Lord
It restricts salvation exclusively to Jews
It denies the authority of the Gentile mission
It advocates Gentile rejection of the gospel
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the word of God turning from Jews to Gentiles as commanded by the Lord
questions.explanation: Verses 46–47 reveal the divine mandate to bring salvation to the Gentiles after Jewish rejection.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 13:30 and 13:34 teach about the resurrection and its effects?
options: God raised Jesus from the dead so He would not undergo decay, securing sure mercies
Resurrection is symbolic without literal meaning
Jesus remained in corruption after resurrection
The resurrection negates all Old Testament promises
questions.correctAnswer: God raised Jesus from the dead so He would not undergo decay, securing sure mercies
questions.explanation: Verse 30 states God raised Jesus, and 34 explains this resurrection ensures no corruption and grants sure mercies.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 13:38 and 13:39 teach about the sufficiency of Christ for salvation?
options: Through Jesus forgiveness and justification are granted, unattainable by the law
Christ's work is incomplete without law observance
Salvation depends on legalistic performance
Forgiveness is independent of faith in Christ
questions.correctAnswer: Through Jesus forgiveness and justification are granted, unattainable by the law
questions.explanation: Both verses emphasize that forgiveness and justification come through Jesus, not by the law.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 13:17 and 13:22 teach about God's providence and covenant faithfulness?
options: God chose and exalted Israel, and raised David as king fulfilling His covenant
God abandoned Israel after Egypt
David's kingship was accidental with no divine purpose
Israel's history is unrelated to God's promises
questions.correctAnswer: God chose and exalted Israel, and raised David as king fulfilling His covenant
questions.explanation: Verse 17 shows God's election of Israel, and 22 shows David's divine appointment, highlighting providence and faithfulness.

questions.question: Skeptics claim the blinding of Elymas in Acts 13:8-11 is a myth. What does this passage actually teach?
options: God actively judges opposition to the gospel through miraculous means
Elymas was simply ignored without consequence
Paul performed magic to deceive the deputy
The event is a parable without historical basis
questions.correctAnswer: God actively judges opposition to the gospel through miraculous means
questions.explanation: Acts 13:8-11 shows God’s judgment manifesting in Elymas’s blindness as a real sign against opposing the gospel.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 13:26 teach about the universal scope of salvation?
options: Salvation is sent to the children of Abraham and all who fear God
Salvation is exclusive to ethnic Jews only
Only Gentiles can receive salvation
Salvation depends on ethnic identity alone
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation is sent to the children of Abraham and all who fear God
questions.explanation: Acts 13:26 addresses both Jews and God-fearing Gentiles, indicating salvation's inclusive reach.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Acts 13:2 specifically demonstrate?
options: Sovereignty in calling workers
Wrath
Immutability
Omnipresence
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty in calling workers
questions.explanation: In Acts 13:2, the Holy Ghost directs the church to separate Barnabas and Saul, showing divine sovereign initiative.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 13:35 and 13:37 teach regarding Christ's resurrection and corruption?
options: Christ did not see corruption unlike David, affirming His divine nature
Both David and Christ experienced corruption equally
Resurrection means immediate ascension without bodily resurrection
David’s resurrection is proof of Christ’s mortality
questions.correctAnswer: Christ did not see corruption unlike David, affirming His divine nature
questions.explanation: Verse 35 says the Holy One would not see corruption, and 37 contrasts David's decay with Christ's incorruption.

questions.question: How does Acts 13:52 contribute to the narrative arc of the early church's growth?
options: The disciples are filled with joy and the Holy Ghost, empowering continued mission
The disciples fall into despair and doubt
The church abandons missionary work
The Holy Spirit is withdrawn from believers
questions.correctAnswer: The disciples are filled with joy and the Holy Ghost, empowering continued mission
questions.explanation: Acts 13:52 shows the joy and Spirit empowerment that sustain the early church's mission.
